title: Chained Beasts Patch Notes: October Hotfix & Roadmap
description: Read Chained Beasts patch notes with confirmed bug fixes, the next balance patch plans, and the latest developer roadmap. Live and planned changes separated.

hero.heading: Chained Beasts Patch Notes and Latest Updates
hero.lead: The October 19–20 developer news confirms a shipped hotfix for multiplayer achievement credit, offline startup and Twitch polls. A separate difficulty balance patch, November progression work and December Update 1.1 were announced as plans—not as additional released fixes.

sections.heading: Latest Chained Beasts Hotfix: Three Confirmed Fixes
paragraphs: Featherweight Games' launch-week news explicitly calls these changes an already released hotfix. The announcement does not provide a numbered patch version or exact build identifier, so we do not invent one. The three fixes address three different problems rather than a sweeping guarantee that all online and offline faults are solved.

Certain multiplayer achievements could previously be awarded only to the lobby host. The studio says this issue was fixed. It does not confirm that every missed award will automatically be granted retroactively; affected players should verify their own accounts.

A launch while offline could become stuck on the opening splash screen. The specific failure has been resolved, according to the developer. Separately, Twitch polls sometimes remained open instead of concluding; that behavior is also listed as fixed.
The Steam community page can show the announcement under October 19 while the Steam store shows October 20 because of time zones. Those are views of the same news item, not two separate hotfixes.

sections.heading: Balance Patch: Announced but Not Confirmed Live
paragraphs: The studio said it expected another update later in launch week to reduce difficulty spikes. Its stated direction was to make single-player slightly easier while making multiplayer slightly harder, except for the final boss. That does not turn these prospective changes into shipped patch notes.

No official exact damage, health, enemy spawn or reward adjustments were specified in that summary. Guides reporting precise new percentages without a later verifiable build should be treated cautiously.

Single-player and multiplayer readers need different context: a solo player may plan around personal positioning and recovery decisions, while an online group has to coordinate chains and movement. Neither group should infer that the forthcoming tuning has already affected the currently installed version.

sections.heading: November Meta Progression and December Update 1.1
paragraphs: For November, the developer plans additional content unlocking and build customization through meta progression. It specifically says this should create variety rather than a long-term grind that simply increases permanent player power. The post describes work in progress, not a feature already installed.

For December, the announced Update 1.1 includes an alternate act set in Rome. The team said details would follow as the release plan narrowed. It did not commit to a precise day, and the October post does not prove the update is live.
Unlike the already fixed bugs, a roadmap promise can move. Check the most recent official Steam news before telling another player that a feature has arrived.

sections.heading: Chained Beasts Update Timeline
paragraphs: October 15, 2026: the game formally released on Steam. Its developer outlined full-release content, including solo and online crossplay, nine battles across three acts ahead of the final encounter, ten difficulties and more than 70 afflictions.

October 19–20, 2026: the next major communication documented launch feedback, three shipped fixes and forthcoming balancing and content plans. These two dates are not different game versions merely because they fall on separate storefront and community calendar displays.
This fan guide is reviewed as of October 20. Its review date is not an automated claim that every subsequent patch has been incorporated.

sections.heading: How to Check for a Newer Chained Beasts Patch
paragraphs: Visit the official Chained Beasts Steam game page, open Update History or community News, and compare the issue description to the most recent developer announcement. Check whether it describes a release that has shipped or a roadmap item still in development.

On your own device, make sure the game client has installed available updates before testing an issue again. If a problem persists, record your platform, approximate build date, whether you were offline or online and the behavior you can reproduce. These general troubleshooting notes are not a game-specific debug command.

title: Chained Beasts Beginner Guide: First Run & Combat Tips
description: Start Chained Beasts with a clear first-run plan covering chain combat, weapons, arena hazards, healing choices, and common beginner mistakes.

hero.heading: Chained Beasts Beginner Guide: Your First Arena Run
hero.lead: Start by reading the current tutorial prompts, checking how your chain can move and keeping a fallback after throwing a weapon. Between fights, read the recovery trade-off before taking a heal. These are practical exercises based on developer-confirmed mechanics, not claims of a personally tested walkthrough.

sections.heading: Before Your First Run: Mode, Controls and Practice Goal
paragraphs: Chained Beasts officially released on October 15, 2026. It supports one to four players, with solo, online cooperative and local co-op options. The launch version added content beyond the earlier demo, so do not blindly follow a pre-release key map or assume every earlier video shows the latest combat behavior.

Steam says controllers are recommended, while same-screen cooperative play requires at least one gamepad on the Steam editions. For all platforms, use the inputs shown in the current game tutorial rather than relying on unverified keyboard or controller bindings from someone else's recording.

Before your first fight, set one modest goal: keep room around pillars, avoid being stranded without a usable weapon or understand a recovery choice. Trying to learn every affliction and every arena trick in one round makes it difficult to identify what helped.

Solo and co-op are not interchangeable practices. A group must coordinate chain direction with other humans; a solo player should first learn the attachment behavior actually shown by the current game.

subsections.heading: Solo preparation
paragraphs: Read the current game's solo controls and identify a safe space after each attack. Do not copy a group maneuver that requires another human player.
bullets: Plan a second weapon or route

subsections.heading: Co-op preparation
paragraphs: Agree on a direction callout and regroup instruction before starting. These are optional teamwork habits, not official in-game commands.
bullets: Know which teammate can still move

sections.heading: Your First Fight: Use the Chain Without Losing Position
paragraphs: The developer says coordinated chains can trip foes and can also tangle around pillars when teammates do not cooperate. The first practical exercise is to look at the line between players, identify which objects might obstruct it and decide where everyone will move before charging.

Choose a controlled engagement instead of treating every enemy as a reason to sprint. If the chain has already wrapped around cover, another aggressive move may make the group's position worse. Stop, communicate and test a more open approach.

The game's official description confirms throwable weapons and warns players to have another available. Before throwing, look for a usable replacement or a safer environmental option. This is a readiness decision, not a claim that any particular weapon always respawns.
Avoid copying unverified damage and stun tables. The current official store listing supports the broad use of weapons, traps and chains, not every detailed formula claimed by third-party tips.

steps.heading: Scan
steps.description: Identify pillars, spikes, pits, opponents and a reachable safe route before committing.

steps.heading: Coordinate
steps.description: In co-op, agree on direction. In solo, use your own current-mode control prompts.

steps.heading: Attack deliberately
steps.description: Use tutorial-confirmed attacks or an environmental opportunity while protecting a fallback.

steps.heading: Review
steps.description: Note one positioning error, weapon loss or successful escape to test next round.

sections.heading: Arena Hazards, Tricks and Crowd Favor
paragraphs: The Steam description mentions spikes, snakes, thrown weapons and creatively using the environment to impress the bloodthirsty crowd. These ideas make terrain part of combat rather than scenery only.

Not every available trick is safe in every encounter. If a hazardous object is positioned beyond several enemies or across the chain's movement path, assess the risk of approaching it before attempting a flashy knockback.

The sources used here do not document a guaranteed crowd-favor score for each action, fixed damage numbers for spikes or a universal best opening attack. Observe the current game feedback rather than building a run around those imaginary values.

sections.heading: Between Battles: Skills, Healing and Afflictions
paragraphs: The launch announcement lists more than 70 skills, more than 70 afflictions and 40-plus items. Those are developer totals, not a full set of mechanics individually recorded here. An early lesson is to read each offer in the current game instead of treating a guide's old item name as universally current.
Some recovery choices bring drawbacks. Before choosing, ask which problem the benefit solves, what visible penalty comes with it and whether the next arena makes the trade dangerous.

Likewise, consider whether a newly offered skill helps your current run. Choosing something solely because an unrelated guide ranks it highly can be less useful than solving your actual lack of movement, defense or equipment.

sections.heading: Five Common First-Run Habits to Review
paragraphs: Watch for five avoidable habits: ignoring the chain route, rushing around pillars, throwing the last easy weapon, accepting recovery without reading its drawbacks and changing too many tactics at once.

These are editorial observations to watch for, not guaranteed events or game achievements. If one occurs, write down the relevant moment and plan a single change next time. This is more informative than pretending every player makes the same errors.

With friends, review communication and shared movement. Alone, focus on your own escape route and between-battle decisions. Check the latest patch notes before assuming a future solo balance change is already affecting the encounter.

A useful closing checklist is: update the game, read current controls, choose solo or co-op, identify hazards, plan your weapon fallback, inspect injuries and review one thing that went wrong or right.

faq.question: What should I do first in Chained Beasts?
faq.answer: Follow the current tutorial, identify an escape route and learn chain movement before attempting elaborate attacks.

faq.question: Can I use beginner tips solo?
faq.answer: Yes, but do not assume a maneuver requiring other human players works the same way alone.

faq.question: How do I use chains in combat?
faq.answer: The developer confirms coordinated chains can trip enemies; use current tutorial prompts for exact inputs.

faq.question: Should I heal after every battle?
faq.answer: No universal rule is confirmed; read the present benefit, drawback and situation.

faq.question: Can I follow old demo controls?
faq.answer: Only after checking your current game because the full release has changed content and may differ by input device.

title: Chained Beasts Crossplay: Platforms & Co-op Guide
description: Does Chained Beasts support crossplay? See confirmed online co-op support, the 1–4 player limit, local play differences, and facts to check before joining.

hero.heading: Chained Beasts Crossplay and Multiplayer Explained
hero.lead: Yes. Chained Beasts officially advertises online crossplay and supports one to four players. Local couch co-op is a separate option. The cited developer notices do not prove every platform pairing, the exact invite-code menu location or cross-save support.

sections.heading: Does Chained Beasts Have Crossplay?
paragraphs: The Steam store explicitly lists Cross-Platform Multiplayer, and the developer's October 15 release news mentions online crossplay. That confirms cross-platform play as a feature. It is not equivalent to a chart guaranteeing that every edition can connect directly to every other edition.

Crossplay is the ability to play online with people using supported different platforms. Cross-progression, by contrast, would mean carrying saves and unlocks between systems. One feature does not establish the other.

Do not mistake 'not verified' for 'not supported.' The responsible answer about a specific platform pair is to check the latest support information for both editions rather than invent a compatibility promise.

sections.heading: Online Co-op, Local Co-op and Player Limits
paragraphs: Steam lists single-player, online co-op, shared-screen play, Remote Play Together and cross-platform multiplayer. These labels describe separate ways to play; one mode's requirements do not automatically carry over to another.

The Steam system requirements state that at least one gamepad is necessary for same-screen co-op. That is a local setup note for Steam editions and does not prove the equivalent controller requirements on every console.

The public announcement does not definitively explain mixed local-and-online parties on each release. Players who require that arrangement should seek a current platform-specific statement rather than assuming a universal party configuration.

sections.heading: Which Platforms Has Featherweight Announced?
paragraphs: The studio's September 2026 press release named Steam, Xbox/Game Pass for Xbox and Windows PC, PlayStation 5 and Nintendo Switch for its October 15 launch. The Steam store identifies Windows and macOS versions directly.

An announced platform launch does not independently confirm regional availability in every digital store or every pair's online compatibility. Avoid presenting a platform list as if it were a documented full-mesh crossplay chart.
Online access, friends lists and subscription rules can vary by platform. This guide does not invent one universal account-linking process or purchasing condition.

sections.heading: Before You Invite Friends: A Practical Checklist
paragraphs: Ask everyone to confirm the edition they own and install the current available update. Agree whether you intend to play online or on the same screen, then check that the total group is no larger than four.

Check each platform's online account or service requirements using that platform's own documentation. If the game displays a lobby problem, record the exact wording and affected editions before trying an unverified workaround.
The steps below are general preparation guidance, not a fabricated screenshot-by-screenshot tour through Chained Beasts' invitation menus.

sections.heading: Multiplayer Update Notes and Related Guides
paragraphs: The October developer hotfix addressed certain achievements being granted only to the multiplayer host. It does not state that every multiplayer connection failure was fixed or that past achievements will be reissued automatically.
For successful group play, the beginner guide offers movement and chain communication exercises. If you decide to play alone instead, the solo guide explains why its planning questions differ.

title: Chained Beasts Solo Guide: Tips & Difficulty Update
description: Play Chained Beasts solo with confirmed single-player facts, combat and healing decisions, plus the latest status of planned solo difficulty changes.

hero.heading: Chained Beasts Solo Guide: Playing Alone
hero.lead: Yes—Chained Beasts supports single-player. The developer's October 19–20 news says solo is intended to become slightly easier in a later balance patch. The announcement does not prove that the future change is already installed or publish exact tuning numbers.

sections.heading: Can You Play Chained Beasts Solo?
paragraphs: The Steam store lists single-player, and the October 15 launch post expressly states that players may fight alone. Solo is part of the official released game, not a fan-made modification or temporary demo-only function.

Chained Beasts is also marketed around friends physically chained together, but that cooperative concept does not cancel its solo support. Players should read the current in-game solo instructions instead of copying a video that assumes two human players are attached.
Some third-party solo pages describe specific ball or anchor behavior. Without a direct verified current build recording, this guide does not present those mechanics as developer-confirmed facts.

An important contrast is the human planning role. In co-op you coordinate a route with other players; solo requires you to choose your own equipment, movement and recovery strategy without expecting another person to call a retreat.

table.caption: Supported modes and editorial planning differences
rows: Planned slightly harder except final boss

sections.heading: Solo Combat: Protect Your Escape Route
paragraphs: Official game material emphasizes weapons, chain physics and environmental hazards. An actionable solo habit is to identify a retreat lane before an attack. This is a planning rule, not an assertion that enemies follow a particular unpublished movement algorithm.

If a large arena obstacle sits behind you, consider repositioning before committing. Throwing a weapon is an official feature, but the developer warns that players should have another available. Without backup equipment, a risky throw may remove an important option for the next exchange.

Observe the situation after each fight: were you trapped by scenery, short of a weapon or carrying an injury that disrupted movement? Writing one specific cause helps more than a generalized 'just dodge more' tip.
The source materials do not establish a universal best weapon, exact boss health, guaranteed drop order or numerical solo damage modifier. Leave those claims for real current-build tests.

subsections.heading: Before the next enemy
paragraphs: Look for a safe lane, usable weapon and a hazard you can avoid. Choose one clear decision to make before any commitment.

subsections.heading: After a difficult fight
paragraphs: Review the cause of danger and change only one relevant habit in the next practice attempt.
bullets: Avoid attributing everything to an unreleased patch

sections.heading: Managing Injuries and Healing Alone
paragraphs: Featherweight describes physical and mental injuries and more than 70 afflictions at launch. Its earlier official update also introduced the Surgeon as a between-acts option for managing afflictions or obtaining skill-granting augmentations at a cost.

The exact result of a treatment should come from the current in-game text. The cited sources do not demonstrate that a named ailment is cured with a fixed success rate or fixed price. A solo player can nevertheless make a useful decision by comparing a displayed immediate benefit to a potentially more disruptive drawback.
Use the recovery worksheet to make your own observations, then revise your plan based on what actually happened. This separates personal experience from an unsupported 'best healing' tier list.

sections.heading: Solo Difficulty: Current Support vs Planned Rebalance
paragraphs: The October news announced solo tuning that would make the mode slightly easier and multiplayer tuning that would make groups slightly harder, excluding the final boss. The changes were described as coming later that week; the post itself is not a release notice for them.

An exact launch date, build number, damage multiplier or revised enemy roster was not supplied. Do not tell players the solo adjustment is already active unless a newer official release record confirms it.

Check the latest Steam community announcements before using any claimed new solo meta. A practical positioning and recovery plan stays helpful regardless of whether a future balance tweak has shipped.

sections.heading: A Three-Run Solo Learning Plan
paragraphs: Practice run one: watch your movement and identify one arena object that blocked a safe retreat. Do not invent a specific enemy or battle order; use whichever encounter appears in your current game.
Practice run two: focus on the weapon you carry, when you throw it and whether there is a backup. A deliberate throw that leaves no plan afterward may be a worse trade than a shorter-range action.
Practice run three: read all recovery choices and write down the actual condition and consequence. Compare the following fight rather than assuming every improvement is caused by upcoming balancing.

This is an original observation worksheet, not an official quest and not a claim that its writer personally completed the three runs. You can adapt it when moving from solo to co-op, but chain communication then becomes a shared responsibility.

title: Chained Beasts Afflictions: Healing & Surgeon Guide
description: Learn how Chained Beasts afflictions affect your run, what healing and surgeon choices trade away, and how to compare verified effects before choosing.

hero.heading: Chained Beasts Afflictions and Healing Guide
hero.lead: Featherweight Games reports over 70 afflictions in Chained Beasts at launch. Injuries and recovery choices can affect a run; the developer says its Surgeon can help manage afflictions or offer skill-granting augmentations at a cost. Specific cure chances and every individual effect are not published in the cited materials.

sections.heading: What Are Chained Beasts Afflictions?
paragraphs: The official game description emphasizes that gladiators endure physical and mental injuries while surviving consecutive fights. The October 15 launch post confirms more than 70 afflictions, but that quantity is not a licensed list of every name, trigger or cure.

Pre-launch official news provides examples of the variety involved. The developer described impaired vision and missing toes as possible affliction-like inconveniences, and a July beta announcement named Psychosis as a condition that made imaginary weapons appear in the arena.

Those examples are grounded in developer statements but were published before full launch. It would be inaccurate to assign them a definitive launch-version percentage, duration or cure without checking the currently released game.

Read the effect shown by your own game as the source of truth for a particular choice. This site explains the framework and distinguishes verified descriptions from the details it has not directly tested.

sections.heading: How Injuries Affect Your Next Fight
paragraphs: A visible injury matters because it may alter what movement, weapons or decisions are practical in the next battle. Not every affliction is necessarily acquired from the same source or removed by the same type of treatment.

The developer has emphasized recovery systems with serious trade-offs. In real play, compare the condition you have with the benefit and drawback shown for the available option instead of selecting the one whose name sounds safest.
Some difficulties are more important for solo than for a communicating group, and vice versa. That is a tactical judgment, not evidence of a different hidden solo affliction table.
Do not assume a single community screenshot documents the complete system; effects may have changed since the demo or beta.

sections.heading: Healing and Afflictions: A Decision Worksheet
paragraphs: Before accepting a remedy, identify the exact condition, read the description of the proposed benefit and note any displayed penalty. Ask whether the next fight will be made safer overall, not merely whether your health rises right away.

A remedy may be helpful without being universally optimal. If the offered trade has a cost, compare it to the danger of remaining injured. The official materials used here do not provide a fixed coin cost, success chance or exhaustive answer for every condition.

Where a player-made effect table relies on a single attempt, it should be labeled as a single observation rather than a guaranteed mechanic. Without an original captured run, this page does not invent names or numbers to complete an artificial tier list.

sections.heading: Chained Beasts Surgeon: What Is Officially Confirmed?
paragraphs: In the July 2026 official 'Head North to Germania' beta news, Featherweight said the Surgeon could be visited between acts. It described two purposes: help manage accumulated afflictions and offer body augmentations that grant skills.
The same post warns that every procedure has a cost. It does not establish that all 70-plus conditions can be removed by this character or that an augmentation is identical to a cure.

Players should inspect the version they are actually playing. A beta description alone cannot support claims about exact release-build prices, menu timing or the results of treating a particular named affliction.

To go deeper than another general guide, use a traceable before-and-after record: capture your affliction screen, the procedure option and the visible result. Only then can a guide responsibly report a specific tested choice.

sections.heading: How to Record Real Affliction Effects
paragraphs: A useful observation entry contains the condition name and complete on-screen wording, mode, game build if visible, offered treatment, displayed trade-off and result in the next fight. One run documents an event but not its probability.
If you plan to compare two remedies, note whether the conditions before treatment were actually comparable. Winning the next fight does not by itself prove a surgeon option raised a hidden stat.

This page deliberately avoids claiming a 70-item complete affliction encyclopedia without direct source evidence. That restraint is important because other sites may present memorable examples, but a copied list cannot validate itself.

For first-time players, the beginner guide helps frame injury choices during early battles. Solo players can use the dedicated solo log. Check official news for updates before relying on mechanics from earlier beta versions.
